sources.title: OECD — Tax policy
sources.note: High-level statement of tax policy aims: revenue, inclusion, and sustainable growth.

sources.title: IFS — Tax by Design (Mirrlees Review)
sources.note: Integrated first-principles review of tax design for an open developed economy.

sources.title: OECD — International VAT/GST Guidelines
sources.note: VAT/GST is designed as a broad-based tax on final consumption.

sources.title: IMF — Designing a Progressive VAT
sources.note: Explores pairing a broad-base VAT with real-time rebates to remove regressivity.

sources.title: IMF — Equity and Efficiency Effects of Land Value Taxation
sources.note: Land value taxation is efficient because the supply of land is inelastic, though distributional design still matters.

sources.title: World Bank — What is Carbon Pricing?
sources.note: Carbon pricing internalizes external costs of greenhouse-gas emissions.

sources.title: World Bank — State and Trends of Carbon Pricing 2025
sources.note: Current global coverage, public-budget revenue, and fiscal-stability context for carbon pricing.

sources.title: OECD — Inheritance Taxation in OECD Countries
sources.note: Inheritance taxation can raise revenue, reduce wealth inequality, and be efficient when well designed.

sources.title: OECD — Global Minimum Tax
sources.note: Official OECD overview of the GloBE framework and recent implementation materials.

sources.title: OECD — Competition in artificial intelligence infrastructure
sources.note: Documents concentration and bottlenecks in AI infrastructure markets.

sources.title: OECD — The impact of Artificial Intelligence on productivity, distribution and growth
sources.note: AI can raise productivity but also worsen concentration and inequality.

sources.title: OECD — Artificial intelligence (topic page)
sources.note: Current adoption trends across OECD economies.

sources.title: IMF — Artificial Intelligence (topic page)
sources.note: IMF framing of AI productivity gains, wage pressure, and distributional questions.

sources.title: IMF — Bridging Skill Gaps for the Future: New Jobs Creation in the AI Age
sources.note: Recent IMF work on new skills, wages, polarization, and AI-related labor change.

sources.title: IEA — Energy and AI
sources.note: Official IEA analysis of AI-linked electricity demand and data-centre growth.

sources.title: NIST — AI Risk Management Framework resources
sources.note: Official NIST entrypoint for AI RMF 1.0 and the Generative AI Profile.

sources.title: NIST — AI Risk Management Framework
sources.note: NIST overview of the AI RMF and Generative AI profile resources.

sources.title: Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy — Distributive Justice
sources.note: Compact philosophical grounding on distributive justice.

sources.title: Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy — Ethics of Artificial Intelligence and Robotics
sources.note: Background on artificial moral agency and moral status questions.

sources.title: Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy — Computing and Moral Responsibility
sources.note: Background on responsibility distribution across humans and technologies.

sources.title: IMF — Taxes in Practice
sources.note: Compact explanation of tax incidence, rent taxation, corporate-tax burden-shifting, and why statutory remittance does not settle who really pays.

sources.title: IMF — Fiscal Policy Can Help Broaden the Gains of AI to Humanity
sources.note: Official IMF blog arguing that AI-era fiscal policy should strengthen social protection, education, and tax design to spread gains and cushion displacement.

sources.title: OECD — Housing Taxation in OECD Countries
sources.note: Housing-tax reforms require careful timing and accompanying tax/transfer measures for vulnerable groups; useful for deferral, gradualism, and liquidity-sensitive reform.

sources.title: OECD — Taxation of Household Savings
sources.note: Useful for timing questions because savings can be taxed at acquisition, holding, and disposal stages rather than through a single annual lens.

sources.title: OECD — Valuation and Assessment of Immovable Property
sources.note: Explains what is valued, how it is valued, and who values it in property-tax systems; useful for revaluation cadence, mass appraisal, and appeal logic.

sources.title: World Bank — Trade-offs in the Design of Simplified Tax Regimes: Evidence from Sub-Saharan Africa
sources.note: Shows the trade-offs simplified small-business regimes face between revenue, simplicity, and equity, and why thresholds and graduation rules matter.

sources.title: OECD — Tax administration
sources.note: High-level support for fair, efficient, effective, rights-aware tax administration and inclusive digital services.

sources.title: OECD — Reallocation of taxing rights to market jurisdictions
sources.note: Official OECD overview of Amount A and the case for giving market jurisdictions a coordinated claim over part of the profits of large multinational firms even without physical presence.

sources.title: IMF — Tax Expenditure Reporting and Its Use in Fiscal Management
sources.note: Treats tax expenditures as alternative means of delivering fiscal support and argues for integrating their cost into fiscal management rather than leaving incentives scattered and hidden.

sources.title: OECD — Fossil fuel support
sources.note: Treats direct transfers and tax expenditures together as support measures and shows how hidden negative taxes can carry large fiscal costs while undermining transition goals.

sources.title: OECD — Taxing Wages 2025
sources.note: Shows that allowances, credits, taxes, and cash benefits together determine final household burdens, helping distinguish floor protection from privilege.

sources.title: OECD — Tax Policy and Gender Equality
sources.note: OECD stocktake of explicit and implicit gender bias in tax systems; highlights second-earner taxation, credits, allowances, and gender-disaggregated data as central tax-design issues.

sources.title: IMF — Gendered Taxes: The Interaction of Tax Policy with Gender Equality
sources.note: Reviews labor, capital, wealth, and consumption taxation through a gender-equality lens and discusses the impact of household taxation on labor supply and tax design.

sources.title: OECD — Beneficial Ownership and Tax Transparency
sources.note: OECD / Global Forum report on why beneficial ownership transparency matters for tax evasion, illicit flows, and effective implementation of tax-transparency standards.

sources.title: FATF — Beneficial Ownership
sources.note: FATF topic page and guidance on adequate, accurate, and up-to-date beneficial ownership information for legal persons and arrangements, useful for anti-fragmentation and real-controller rules.

sources.title: OECD — Tax certainty and policy implementation
sources.note: OECD topic page treating tax certainty as a fundamental goal tied to stability, predictability, dispute prevention, and efficient tax administration.

sources.title: IMF — Tax Law Design and Drafting, Chapter 2: Legal Framework for Taxation
sources.note: IMF legal-design discussion distinguishing retroactive tax laws from prospective operation and explaining why tax legislation is usually designed to operate largely prospectively.

sources.title: OECD — Enhancing Simplicity to Foster Tax Certainty and Growth
sources.note: OECD 2025 report arguing that simplification and multilateral co-operation can increase tax certainty and reduce unnecessary complexity in policy and rule design.

sources.title: OECD — Collection: Tax Administration 2025
sources.note: OECD 2025 collection chapter stressing customer-service approaches for short-term cash-flow problems, early engagement, and proportionate enforcement in tax debt management.

sources.title: OECD — Privacy and data protection
sources.note: OECD topic page grounding privacy as tied to safety, dignity, and fundamental rights, and warning that government access to personal data cannot be unconstrained or unreasonable.

sources.title: IMF — Legislating for Fair and Effective Tax Collection
sources.note: IMF 2025 note arguing that forced collection powers require adequate safeguards, prompt recourse, and staged, proportionate use of intrusive recovery tools.

sources.title: OECD — Disputes: Tax Administration 2025
sources.note: OECD 2025 disputes chapter listing common taxpayer rights and emphasizing effective challenge processes, review, and checks on tax powers.

sources.title: OECD — Open government and citizen participation
sources.note: OECD topic page on participation, voice, transparency, and trust in public institutions; useful for the archive's claim that direct civic burdens need some channel of representation or proxy voice.

sources.title: OECD — AI in tax administration: Governing with Artificial Intelligence
sources.note: OECD 2025 chapter stating that AI-supported tax decisions need to be explainable, transparent, and accountable because taxpayers must be able to challenge them.

sources.title: OECD — Laws and policies for combatting discrimination and promoting equality and inclusion
sources.note: Defines direct and indirect discrimination, protected grounds, and explains why apparently neutral rules can still disadvantage protected groups; useful for tax-status-proxy analysis.

sources.title: OHCHR — Economic, social and cultural rights
sources.note: States that laws, policies, and practices can be discriminatory in effect regardless of intent, and that taxation and social transfers may be required to protect marginalized groups.

sources.title: IMF — Should Tax Be King? The Debate over Tax Priority in Insolvency
sources.note: IMF 2025 paper reviewing legal techniques used to protect tax claims in insolvency, and the arguments for and against granting tax priority.

sources.title: OECD — Design of insolvency regimes across countries
sources.note: OECD paper on insolvency-regime design, priority ordering, and the need for predictable ranking rules even where some stakeholders receive special treatment.

sources.title: UNCITRAL — Table of concordance between the Legislative Guide on Insolvency Law and the Recommendations
sources.note: UNCITRAL guidance emphasizing preservation of the insolvency estate and clear rules for ranking priority claims.

sources.title: OECD — Loss carryover provisions
sources.note: Explains that perfect intertemporal loss offsets are necessary for neutrality across projects with different risk profiles and documents how carry-forwards, carry-backs, inflation indexation, and offset limits affect tax symmetry and stabilisation.

sources.title: OECD — Tax incentives for research and development: Corporate Tax Statistics 2025
sources.note: Shows that refunds and carry-over provisions are common ways to support firms with insufficient tax liability and that refundability can align treatment across profitable and loss-making firms while no such provisions can wipe out benefits in loss years.

sources.title: OECD — Corporate Loss Utilisation through Aggressive Tax Planning
sources.note: Documents aggressive tax-planning risks around corporate losses, including artificial losses, multiple deductions of the same economic loss, and related rules needed to distinguish genuine downside from abuse.

sources.title: OECD — Principle 2: Keep L&P proportionate to risks
sources.note: OECD 2025 guidance saying ex ante licensing and permitting should be used where activities cannot be regulated effectively ex post and where potential harm is significant and irreversible; useful for distinguishing taxation from permission.

sources.title: NIST — AI RMF Playbook: Govern
sources.note: NIST playbook guidance on defining risk tolerances, approval / conditional approval / disapproval, early decommissioning, and governance for AI systems whose risks may outrun the ability to reasonably mitigate them.

sources.title: OECD — Taxing Wages 2023: Indexation of Labour Taxation and Benefits in OECD Countries
sources.note: Explains automatic and discretionary indexation, fiscal drag, and how inflation can erode the real value of tax thresholds and benefits.

sources.title: IMF — Tax Distortions from Inflation: What are They? How to Deal with Them?
sources.note: Shows how inflation can create phantom gains, distort effective tax rates, and erode depreciation allowances and other real-value protections.

sources.title: IMF — Inflation Indexation in Public Finances: A Global Dataset on Current Practices
sources.note: Cross-country evidence on current indexation practices, showing that taxes are often less indexed than major spending items and therefore can drift distributively during inflation.

sources.title: OECD — Tax Policy Reforms 2025
sources.note: Documents recent country practice in adjusting thresholds, allowances, credits, and other nominal tax parameters in response to inflation and price pressure.

sources.title: OECD — Recommendation of the Council on Public Policy Evaluation
sources.note: OECD legal instrument calling on governments to establish robust institutions and practices that promote the use of public policy evaluations.

sources.title: OECD — Implementation Toolkit for the OECD Recommendation on Public Policy Evaluation
sources.note: Practical OECD 2025 toolkit on evaluation capacity, continuous learning, and evidence-informed policymaking.

sources.title: OECD — Regulating for the future: OECD Regulatory Policy Outlook 2025
sources.note: Emphasizes adapt-and-learn regulatory processes, feedback loops, anticipatory governance, and ex post review with practical recommendations for amendment, replacement, or removal.

sources.title: NIST — AI RMF Playbook: Manage
sources.note: NIST guidance on regular monitoring, risk-tolerance review, post-deployment feedback, incident response, and decommissioning for AI systems that drift or exceed tolerated risk.

sources.title: OECD — Strengthening productivity and the Single Market
sources.note: Notes that clear benchmarks and sunset clauses help prevent inefficiencies and policy capture, useful for temporary or experimental tax instruments and negotiated support packages.

sources.title: OECD — Modernising Access to Social Protection
sources.note: OECD 2024 report saying automatic enrolment using linked administrative data can increase benefit take-up by relieving recipients from the burden of applying.

sources.title: OECD — Services: Tax Administration 2025
sources.note: OECD 2025 services chapter saying administrations support compliance by making it easier to understand obligations, report taxable income, and make payments, useful for low-friction claiming and delivery design.

sources.title: OECD — Assessment: Tax Administration 2025
sources.note: OECD 2025 assessment chapter on prefilled returns, e-channels, and efforts to reduce burdens in high-volume filing, notice, refund, and payment processes.
